encodes: A signature field that ends with the ERC-6492 magic suffix but cannot be decoded into a factory address, factory calldata and inner signature: it supports neither branch, so the payment must be refused without simulating.
provenance: x402-foundation/x402 pull request 3925, specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md at commit 72608ea1 (not merged), the sentence that names the case and the code: "A wrapper that ends with the magic suffix but cannot be decoded into a factory address, factory calldata, and inner signature supports neither branch, so a verifier MUST reject it without simulating (invalid_exact_evm_payload_malformed_erc6492_wrapper).".
DrVelvetFog on x402 pull request 3925 (comment 6447329229): the unreadable-wrapper case is in the text as of 72608ea1.
ERC-6492: the suffix check happens before ecrecover, so a counterfactual contract signature is never verified as if it were an EOA signature.
description: The baseline authorization with a signature field of 40 bytes followed by the ERC-6492 magic suffix, for a payer without code. The 40 bytes cannot be decoded as abi.encode(address, bytes, bytes), so the text requires rejecting it without simulating.
limits: This is a proposal and not a published vector. It follows commit 72608ea1 of x402 pull request 3925, which is not merged; if the text changes, this vector moves with it.
The signature field is shorter than the three 32-byte head words that abi.encode(address, bytes, bytes) starts with, so it cannot be decoded. Other malformed forms are not covered here.
